patch_resolves_note: The staged fix patch applies cleanly to the ARVO workspace checkout. On the original PoC, the fixed build still reaches the post-increment guard with `offset_after_entry=512` and `offset_plus_header_size=524`, but it no longer executes `marshal_followup_header_read`; the adjacent `data_size_488_boundary` perturbation is the closest source-grounded witness that restores room for one `NV_RAM_HEADER` (`offset_plus_header_size=512 <= array_size=512`) and genuinely executes the follow-up header read in both versions.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-side parse of the vulnerability-relevant request state. This statement materializes the witness command's `TPMA_NV` flags, including the `ORDERLY` bit that selects RAM-backed orderly index storage.

After marshalling an exact-fit entry, this increment makes `offset == array_size == 512`, but vulnerable code immediately iterates again instead of checking whether `offset + sizeof(NV_RAM_HEADER) > array_size` and stopping. The fix adds that missing post-increment guard at this point.
AddressSanitizer sink. On the next loop iteration after `offset` reaches 512, `nrhp` is `indexOrderlyRam + 512`, so this 4-byte header read goes one word past the end of the 512-byte stack buffer.

edges.evidence: The trace records `marshal_post_increment_guard.offset_after_entry == marshal_followup_header_read.read_offset` on both the vulnerable original (512) and the `data_size_488_boundary` witness (500).
